decision: Use a tracking-only roadmap plus executable child plans.
rationale: The visual operating console spans local dashboard UX, action modeling, projection adapters, architecture views, and optional realtime adapters. Keeping the roadmap tracking-only prevents V1/V2 scope from leaking into the V0 operator console child.

decision: Audience-lock V0 to the operator actively driving the loop.
rationale: The dashboard has at least four audiences. V0 must answer 'what needs me now?' rather than trying to serve operator oversight, audit review, newcomer explanation, and shared team operation at once.

decision: Local-first dashboard is core; Firebase remains V2 adapter work.
rationale: The bundled static dashboard and state projection already work without Firebase. V0 must not expose Firebase toggles or placeholders; realtime mutation belongs behind governed adapter paths after firebase-dashboard F003/F005 close.

decision: Define a shared ActionItem provider and four-band status taxonomy before rendering the operator view.
rationale: Without a common action/status model, gates, capabilities, reconcile drift, and supervisors would each invent different next-action language and colors. The provider model is the substrate that makes the dashboard an operating console rather than a pile of cards.

Architecture HTML is useful for newcomer/auditor/overview contexts, but it does not help the in-loop operator decide what to do next. V0 may surface an architecture-stale action; the visual architecture page is V1.
